verified_claims: OS Terrain 50 is an Open Data lower-resolution digital terrain model for Great Britain.
Grid and contour products are created from the same source data but have different representations.
Supply tiles are 10km by 10km and are named from the National Grid reference of the south-west corner.
Grid data uses regular 50m posts and contour data uses 10m contour intervals.
Grid downloads contain ASCII height data plus GML metadata, projection and auxiliary files.
The ASCII header declares 200 columns, 200 rows and 50m cell size.
Rows run west to east and subsequent rows progress southward from the north-west tile origin.
Each grid value is calculated at the centre of its 50m pixel.
Height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1m.
The GML file provides location, spacing, vertical-reference and spatial-reference metadata for the external ASCII data block.
Per-tile GEMINI metadata includes tile reference and information such as flying date.
GML feature and geometry identifiers are unique within a product release.
Geometry identifiers use a .geom suffix.
Whole-tile refresh regenerates sequential identifiers and no feature-level change-only update is planned.
GML geometry CRS is expressed as EPSG:27700 in an OGC URN.
Spot heights are automated selections and can be lower than surrounding contours for genuine depressions.
Contour spot-height z values are rounded to whole metres and are not equivalent to grid-cell values.
A tile metadata statistic is not a candidate-specific cell measurement.
Exact row and column selection requires verified tile bytes, header values and pixel-centre addressing.
No official TQ29 binary archive, SHA or candidate cell values were retrieved in this wave.
No OS Terrain 50 value can be promoted as an exact candidate elevation without byte-level readback.
